## Appearance

Anne is a pale girl with a pointed face and large, solemn gray eyes, which are also described as luminous. She has a freckled face, including seven tiny, persistent freckles on her nose, and an oval cheek that flushes faintly with pink. Her hair is naturally red, worn at times in long braids or flowing unbraided in a torrent of brightness, though friends sometimes refer to it as auburn. Her hair has also been cut short into silky curls after being closely shingled, and it was briefly green during one incident.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P0](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0000), [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P12](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0012), [v1 CHAPTER VIII. ## Personality

A passionate, imaginative, and serious-minded individual, she possesses a strong will, deep personal loyalty, and a keen romantic nature. Though smart, obedient, and quick to learn, her heedless and impulsive temperament often leads her to fall into daydreams mid-task. She experiences intense emotional shifts, frequently flying high on the wings of anticipation before crashing down into despair. Academically ambitious, her motivations include excelling in her studies to win a scholarship, making a proud impression, and ultimately attending college to become a teacher. She also aspires to emulate those she admires and strives to add beauty to the world around her. Creatively skilled in storytelling, singing, and interacting with children, she nevertheless harbors a distinct fear of entering the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood) after dark.

## History

Anne Shirley was taken in as an orphan by [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) and [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), where she quickly formed a lifelong friendship with [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) and began attending the local school. After [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) teased her about her hair, she smashed her slate over his head and refused to speak to him, though she later forgave him in secret during their intense academic rivalry. Anne continued to reside in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) for six years, during which she frequently engaged in imaginative misadventures, such as inventing ghosts in the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood) with [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) and mistakenly serving her friend currant wine. Over the years, [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) bought her a long-desired dress with puffed sleeves for a concert, and Anne eventually earned top honors on the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination. When [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) suddenly passed away and [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) faced potential blindness, Anne chose to forfeit her college scholarship to remain at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables), leading [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) to give up the local teaching post so she could take it. As the village schoolteacher, she organized the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers), accidentally sold her neighbor Mr. Harrison's cow before making amends, and helped [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) raise two young twins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md). Through her teaching and social calls, she befriended local figures such as Miss [Lavendar Lewis](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) and eventually reconnected Miss [Lavendar](../character/lavendar-lewis.md) with her former suitor, [Stephen Irving](../character/stephen-irving.md). Years after their initial schoolroom clash, Anne permanently ended her feud with [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), coming to regard him as a close friend while preparing for her ultimate departure to [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college).

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER III. Marilla Cuthbert Is Surprised P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER III. ## Quotes

> "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P11](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0011)

> "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P43](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0043)

> "I love pretty things; and I hate to look in the glass and see something that isn’t pretty. It makes me feel so sorrowful—just as I feel when I look at any ugly thing. I pity it because it isn’t beautiful."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P45](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0045)

> "I love Green Gables already, and I never loved any place before. No place ever seemed like home. Oh, Marilla, I’m so happy. I could pray right now and not find it a bit hard."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P49](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0049)

> "Oh, Marilla, I’m frightened—now that it has come I’m actually frightened. What if she shouldn’t like me! It would be the most tragical disappointment of my life."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P10](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0010)

### [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--diana-barry.md)

Anne and [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) are bosom friends who swore a solemn oath of friendship after meeting at [Orchard Slope](../codex/places.md#orchard-slope). They act as playmates who row together on the pond, attend school and parties together, and share deep emotional confidences. Their close bond is marked by intense mutual affection, such as Anne weeping at the mere thought of [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) marrying and leaving her.

### [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Anne and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) began as bitter academic rivals and enemies after he pulled her braid and called her 'Carrots,' leading Anne to smash a slate over his head and maintain a persistent grudge. Over time, Anne secretly forgave him and they eventually became close friends, literary collaborators writing newspaper notes together, and study partners. Unknown to Anne, [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) harbors romantic feelings for her.

### [Josephine Barry](../character/josephine-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--josephine-barry.md)

Great-[Aunt Josephine](../character/josephine-barry.md) and Anne initially met under tense circumstances when Anne accidentally jumped onto her bed while staying at Diana's house. After Anne courageously visited her to offer a heartfelt confession, [Miss Barry](../character/josephine-barry.md) was charmed and amused by her, transforming the encounter into a firm friendship. The two visit each other, and [Miss Barry](../character/josephine-barry.md) frequently hosts Anne and offers her encouragement.
